ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.32593v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: What if an explanation achieves perfect scores but it is uninterpretable? We show that this happens when explaining audio deepfake detectors. Using an optimization-based method, we explain a state-of-the-art wav2vec2-based detector. The explanations achieve optimal scores on standard explainability metrics, i.e. fidelity and faithfulness. Visual inspection, however, reveals unintuitive and uninterpretable patterns. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.32910v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech enhancement for spatial audio needs to improve speech quality and intelligibility while preserving the spatial characteristics of the acoustic scene. Time-frequency masking provides an effective approach for speech enhancement, but its performance and spatial fidelity may depend strongly on the signal representation in which the mask is applied. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.32023v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: AI-generated music has become common on music streaming platforms, and listeners often cannot distinguish it from music made by humans. AI-music detection is therefore needed, but detectors trained on a fixed set of generators often fail on unseen generators. arXiv:2611.32286v1 Announce Type: cross

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29557v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Evaluating speech-to-speech translation (S$2$ST) systems requires assessing multiple dimensions of translated speech, including semantic adequacy, speaker similarity, and acoustic naturalness. Existing approaches are largely text-based, relying on ASR transcripts and primarily assessing semantic adequacy, while other dimensions require separate metrics. We propose S$2$SCORE, a unified text-free evaluation framework that jointly models these dimensions within a multi-task architecture and produces a human-calibrated overall quality score. S$2

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.30723v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Speech language models (LMs) generate speech as sequences of discrete tokens, requiring tokenizers that preserve both acoustic detail and linguistic content at a low bitrate. Semanticenhanced tokenizers may discard acoustic detail, whereas acousticoriented tokenizers retain acoustic variation that hinders language modeling. Unified tokenizers combine both, but encoding them within a single feature space can cause interference, and existing methods typically align acoustic features to fixed targets from a frozen semantic teacher. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: PairAlign: A Framework for Autoregressive Tokenization via Self-Alignment with Applications to Audio Tokenization
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2605.06582v5 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Modern learning systems represent perceptual signals with continuous vectors, but comparison, retrieval, memory, alignment, and reasoning are often symbolic. In language, tokens provide this interface; for speech and audio, it must be learned. Existing audio tokenizers rely on local quantization, clustering, or reconstruction, leaving sequence consistency, compactness, length, termination, and edit geometry only indirectly controlled. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: GigaEdge Enhance: An SDK for Practical Streaming Speech Enhancement
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.13243v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We present GigaEdge Enhance, an open source SDK for streaming speech enhancement on CPU servers, mobile devices, and in browsers. Applications can build enhancement channels from neural denoising, normalization and dynamics blocks, sample rate conversion, and acoustic echo cancellation where supported. These stages can be combined, while normalization can also run with out a neural model. The release includes an 8 kHz INT8 denoiser and discriminative and hybrid 48 kHz FP32 models. A shared C++ core supports ONNX Runtime and TensorFlow

Abstract: What music can a text-to-music model actually make? The answer to this question has consequences for individual creators, communities, and musical culture more broadly. We introduce MADlibs, a framework to measure the expressive support of state-of-the-art music generators: the subset of musical behaviors they will actually produce across the space of prompts. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.32457v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Layer-wise analyses of frozen self-supervised encoders are used to locate spoofing information in audio deepfake detection. On the ASVspoof 2019 logical access (LA) benchmark, bonafide recordings carry longer leading and trailing silence than spoofed ones, and detectors exploit this cue, the silence shortcut. This paper examines whether layer rankings for a frozen WavLM Base encoder survive the trimming of this silence. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.32458v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing video-to-audio (V2A) methods have achieved promising results in synthesizing high-quality audios. However, as V2A advances toward more flexible user-directed creation, existing methods remain notably limited in controlling the distinct acoustic identities of multiple events within a video. We therefore formulate multi-event reference-conditioned V2A (Mr-V2A), where each event is assigned a specific audio reference and target time span. Mr-V2A presents three key challenges. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.32641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Balrogg, a lossless recompressor that replaces the entropy coding of Ogg Vorbis and Ogg Opus files with adaptive context mixing models. For Vorbis, we write each represent each codebook entry as a tuple of small signed integers (digits), binarized in five stages, and mixed with a direct context model, a bit-history model, and a match model, with weights selected by the neighboring digits and the previous residue pass. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.31301v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips fro

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: BEARING: Who Is Talking to Whom? Grounding Acoustic Direction in Vision for Online Multi-Party Conversation
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.31735v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Understanding a group conversation means deciding, from video and audio, who is speaking and to whom. Leading systems treat these tasks offline on single-channel clips and align models with a self-evaluation reward. We propose BEARING, a geometry-first alternative built on one measured signal: the direction from which a microphone array beside the camera hears a sound. A label-free calibration learned from the stream registers this direction into the camera image, and an online registry of faces, voices and directions needs no enrollment. The

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.32311v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Immersive scene modeling requires synchronized visual and auditory observations under changing viewpoints and scene conditions. Obtaining such observations and references for controlled scene changes remains challenging. We introduce SynAVID, a synthetic audio-visual immersive dataset comprising eight indoor and outdoor scenes. Each minute-scale episode combines fixed camera arrays and moving trajectories with synchronized, viewpoint-dependent binaural audio. Shared scene dynamics, sound-source events, and observer poses drive visual rendering

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.33153v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Jamaica Suk, producer, DJ, and friend, has died
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
We lost Jamaica Suk yesterday, the singular musical force. To say this hits close to home is an understatement; few people have been a better friend or a greater inspiration. My thoughts are with her family, in particular, right now. Music in the end is just an excuse to spend some time together and share some hopes and dreams. Take care of one another. Here's the official statement.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Photophore 2, a 100-oscillator iOS/AUv3 flock synth twelve years in the making
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Photophore renders a swarm of one hundred oscillators as a flock navigating a three-dimensional habitat. First seen on CDM in 2014, version 2 of Taika Systems' instrument adds AUv3 support on iOS -- and parameters modeling predators, hunger, and fear. The result is lush, nuanced layers of sound, pads to leads, that feels uniquely alive.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Nine Inch Nails fans can now stream nearly 2000 live recordings
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
NIN fans, it's a momentous week. For nearly 20 years, the Nine Inch Nails archive has been compiling live shows from 1988 to today; that's now nearly 2000 recordings of over 1200 concerts. The site is a pleasure to navigate now, and this week came big news: streaming, on demand.

The post Nine Inch Nails fans can now stream nearly 2000 live recordings appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Korg’s phase8 acoustic synthesizer adds companion app, updated firmware
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Korg's phase8 remains an acoustic, resonating fascination, just at a time when everything seems lost in a sea of software. The companion app we saw first at Berlin's Superbooth is now public this week, expanding sequencing capabilities and providing tools for arranging and storing ideas, alongside tweaked device firmware.

The post Korg’s phase8 acoustic synthesizer adds companion app, updated firmware appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Seek sick sets from SITKA, Zuggamasta, hellocatfood, in cables and code
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
It may seem the world is closing in, the internet is dying, tides of slop are rising -- don't believe it. The underground shares signs of hope, from Kyiv's SITKA to Köln's Zuggamasta to Earth's hellocatfood. It's got modules. It's got (entirely human!) coding. It's got trippy visuals. The underground resists, nerd style, and it's all happening thanks to the Fediverse and the fantastic Brighton-based Gravitons.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Berlin’s largest electronic music venue, now a stage for debuting military AI
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Berlin Kraftwerk, the former power plant in Berlin Mitte associated with Tresor and Ohm, was the venue last week for Helsing's launch of new agentic technology, Clarity. This platform uses the same controversial AI-driven approach implicated in accelerating the use of flawed intelligence and killing civilians in Palestine, Lebanon, and Iran. Kraftwerk's Head of Sales has taken sole responsibility and apologized. But the fiasco seems emblematic of Berlin's pivot from cultural capital to military-industrial capital, with the money that follows.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Ryo Fujimoto, performing live in Tokyo, asks how to be in an age of violence
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
The masterful artist Ryo Fujimoto works in electronics not just as a passive actor behind machines, but fully embodied in physicality, voice, and sometimes screams. He sends his latest live performance -- an arresting, but ultimately healing performance that takes on war and violence in a powerful machine-vocal cry.

The post Ryo Fujimoto, performing live in Tokyo, asks how to be in an age of violence appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Harps with flowers that bloom and more fanciful creations of Monique Evette
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
If you don't know her work, computer scientist Monique "Evette" Byars has built spectacular, animated instruments, merging digital modeling and fabrication techniques. Flowers bloom. Guitars are reimagined as koi ponds. Sounds get transformed into wearable resin structures. It's enough to make you want to up your airbrush, math, and science games.

The post Harps with flowers that bloom and more fanciful creations of Monique Evette appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Reading Rainbow, the Buchla synth’s “MARF,” and a prototype’s live debut
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Hold on for a wormhole between different nerd universes. Steve Horelick, the prolific composer behind the music for Reading Rainbow, meets the classic Buchla 200, meets a new prototype of an official recreation of the Multiple Arbitrary Function Generator (MARF). Also, Star Trek. Let's explain what those things are for those who don't know -- and talk about how you can join a special event live online.

Ableton Live 13 is now in limited public beta. That includes a lot of what you've asked for, like multi-band Racks, overhauled preset navigation, and ARA 2 support for tools like Melodyne. And it's packed with new goodies: a very Ableton step sequencer, a multi-engine Drum Synth with some nice twists, new effects, a new ambient looper, and more. Also, I know some of you will like this: no mention of AI. It's like we just get to talk about music-making tools again.
